Thanks Jonas — Thurs 10/15 10:00 PT works for us. A few clarifying notes in advance so we can be efficient on the call:

1) Region: primary will be us-west-2, but we run significant EU inference from eu-west-1 during business hours; happy to have eu as DR but would like warm-fallback to eu for predictable bursts (not cold start).

2) Traffic profile: baseline 150 rps, usually in 20–30 small spikes up to 450 rps for ~10–15 minutes (model cache prefix reuse is common). Seasonal loads (batch jobs) run overnight — can be re-routed to lower-cost pools.

3) SLA expectations: 99.9% p95 latency target with automatic fallback to hosted model variant on sustained resource constraint. Procurement will also request retention/visibility on audit logs for 6 months.

Ill attach our internal ops contact to the call — Claire — and procurement is looped. See you at 10:00 PT.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
Peregrine Labs

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation: Peregrine Labs — Dedicated GPU Provision & Traffic Plan

Alex / team — great notes. Ive captured the baseline and spike profile and sketched a recommended autoscale + warm-burst approach that balances cost and headroom. See summary below and attached spreadsheet (peregrine_capacity_matrix.xlsx).

Recommended default policy (can be tuned post-activation):
- Base pool: 6 GPUs (pinned).
- Autoscale threshold: add 2 GPUs when 75% average GPU util over 60s across pool; add another 2 GPUs at sustained 85% over 120s.
- Warm-burst: pre-warm up to 6 additional GPUs for predicted diurnal spikes; warm-burst will remain idle but with shortened spin-up (KV cache snapshotting enabled).
- Fallback routing: if pool cannot satisfy requests for >120s, traffic routes to a compatible hosted variant (lower-cost, latency SNOW fallback) with a header indicating fallback_reason.

Operational notes:
- EU fallback: we recommend a small eu-standby capacity (2 GPUs) with KV cache seeding from us-west during low-traffic windows; if youd prefer fully warmed EU fallback we can size that separately (higher cost).
- Audit logs: we can retain request+trace for 6 months (fulfills procurement ask); Ill include the retention statement in SOW.

Attachments: peregrine_capacity_matrix.xlsx (capacity/latency sims), redwood_activation_checklist.pdf

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm acceptance of base/warm-burst sizing and EU fallback preference.
2) Procurement: review SOW doc Ill share tomorrow (dl-4387-sow-v1.docx).
3) Jonas / Marissa: run the CS kickoff and capture any model-level quirks for compaction/quant options.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
